_readme: This file drives the Claim Navigator's recommendation engine. It is plain data, not code — an admin can edit it (via /admin/rules for the weights, or directly in this file) without touching the application. 'options' are the five possible paths. 'problemWeights' and 'statusWeights' score each option based on what the specialist selects; the engine sums the weights for everything selected and ranks the options highest-to-lowest. 'nextStepTemplates' are the narrative blocks shown for whichever option comes out on top, with {{carrier}}, {{damageType}}, and {{problems}} filled in from the specialist's inputs. Scores are 0-3 per tag: 0 = not relevant, 1 = worth considering, 2 = commonly the right call, 3 = strongly indicated.

options.label: Request Reinspection
whenAppropriate: Damage may have been missed during the original inspection
New documentation has become available since the inspection
The original inspection was incomplete or rushed
There is a reasonable, documented basis for another look

options.label: Push the Existing Estimate
whenAppropriate: The damage is already documented and in the file
The carrier has already acknowledged the loss itself
The dispute is really about scope, quantity, or pricing — not coverage
No new inspection or new evidence is needed to make the case

options.label: Appraisal
whenAppropriate: There is a genuine dispute over the amount of loss (not whether it's covered)
The claim has reached a point where standard negotiation is exhausted
Reinspection or supplement requests have stalled without resolving the amount
The gap between our estimate and the carrier's estimate isn't closing

options.label: Gather Additional Documentation
whenAppropriate: The file is missing something a decision-maker would reasonably want to see
A specific carrier objection could be answered directly with the right evidence
Material, code, or matching questions need a authoritative source, not just an opinion
You're not yet ready to escalate or invoke appraisal because the case isn't fully built

options.label: Escalate Internally
whenAppropriate: The claim value or complexity is high
The carrier is disputing the process itself, not just the amount
The client is uncooperative, hostile, or a relationship risk
You're facing a scenario this tool and your playbooks don't clearly cover

reinspection.title: Request Reinspection
reinspection.what: Request that the carrier send an adjuster back out for a reinspection{{onDamageType}}.
reinspection.why: Based on what you entered{{forCarrier}}, there's a reasonable basis to believe the original inspection didn't capture the full picture{{onProblems}}.
beforeYouStart: Confirm your photos clearly show the disputed damage
Review the original estimate line by line
Identify exactly what was omitted or undervalued
Gather any supporting documentation you already have
steps: Send the reinspection request
Clearly identify the disputed items, not just "please look again"
Attach supporting documentation
Log the request in Contractors Cloud
Set a follow-up reminder
gather: Any prior correspondence about the omission
reinspection.document: Log the reinspection request, what was disputed, and any response in Contractors Cloud.
reinspection.followUp: 2-3 weeks if you haven't heard back
reinspection.ifFails: If reinspection is denied or comes back unchanged, review whether the dispute is better suited for appraisal or another escalation path — see the Reinspection and Appraisal playbooks.

pushEstimate.title: Push the Existing Estimate
pushEstimate.what: Go back to the carrier with a clear, itemized case for the existing estimate{{onDamageType}} rather than requesting a new inspection.
pushEstimate.why: The loss itself doesn't appear to be in dispute{{forCarrier}} — this looks like a scope, quantity, or pricing disagreement{{onProblems}}, which usually doesn't need a new inspection to resolve.
beforeYouStart: Confirm the carrier has already acknowledged the loss
Line up your estimate against theirs item by item
Identify exactly where and why the numbers diverge
Check pricing/measurement sources you can cite (e.g. Xactimate, manufacturer specs)
steps: Send a written breakdown of the disputed line items
Explain the basis for each one (code, manufacturer spec, measurement, pricing source)
Ask directly for a revised estimate or a written explanation of the difference
Log the request in Contractors Cloud
Set a follow-up reminder
gather: Manufacturer or code documentation for disputed items
pushEstimate.document: Log the comparison sent, the reasoning given, and the carrier's response in Contractors Cloud.
pushEstimate.followUp: 1-2 weeks if you haven't heard back
pushEstimate.ifFails: If the carrier holds their position without a substantive response, this is a strong candidate for appraisal — see the Appraisal playbook.

appraisal.title: Consider Appraisal
appraisal.what: Evaluate whether this claim is ready to move into appraisal{{onDamageType}}.
appraisal.why: Standard negotiation appears to be stalling on the amount of loss{{forCarrier}}{{onProblems}} rather than on whether the loss is covered at all — that's the situation appraisal exists for.
beforeYouStart: Confirm the disagreement is genuinely about amount, not coverage
Confirm other reasonable attempts to close the gap have been made
Review the policy's appraisal clause for this carrier if available
Loop in your lead if this is a high-value or complex claim
steps: Notify the client and explain what appraisal means in plain terms
Select an appraiser and prepare the demand package
Send the demand letter to formally invoke the appraisal clause
Track the carrier's response and appraiser selection
Log the decision to move to appraisal in Contractors Cloud
gather: Any prior correspondence showing negotiation was attempted
appraisal.who: Carrier, plus your lead if this is a first appraisal or a high-value claim
appraisal.document: Log the decision to invoke appraisal, the date, and the reasoning in Contractors Cloud.
appraisal.followUp: Per the Appraisal playbook — 2-3 weeks with your appraiser once appraisal is underway
appraisal.ifFails: If the carrier disputes the appraisal process itself or the claim gets more complicated than usual, escalate to your lead.

documentation.title: Gather Additional Documentation
documentation.what: Build out the file with documentation that directly answers the carrier's stated objection{{onDamageType}}.
documentation.why: The strongest move here is making the case airtight before pushing further{{forCarrier}}{{onProblems}} — a well-documented file often resolves a dispute without needing reinspection or appraisal at all.
beforeYouStart: Identify exactly what the carrier is disputing or citing as their reason
Figure out what kind of evidence would directly answer that specific objection
Check whether that evidence already exists somewhere in the file
steps: Gather the specific documentation type needed (see Gather below)
Attach it to a clear written explanation of what it shows and why it matters
Send it to the carrier as a reconsideration request
Log it in Contractors Cloud
Set a follow-up reminder
gather: ITEL / RLS / NTS report if a material issue
documentation.who: Carrier / adjuster, and the client if they need to provide anything
documentation.document: Log what was gathered, what it shows, and the date it was sent in Contractors Cloud.
documentation.followUp: 1-2 weeks if you haven't heard back
documentation.ifFails: If the documentation doesn't move the carrier, revisit whether reinspection or appraisal is the better next path.

escalation.title: Escalate Internally
escalation.what: Loop in your lead or manager on this claim before taking the next external step{{onDamageType}}.
escalation.why: Something about this situation — value, complexity, an unresponsive party, or a scenario outside the standard playbooks{{onProblems}} — calls for another set of eyes before you go further{{forCarrier}}.
beforeYouStart: Write a short summary of what's happened and what you've already tried
Be specific about what decision or input you need
Have the claim file ready to share
steps: Message your lead with the summary and the specific question
Share the claim file / Contractors Cloud link
Log that you escalated, to whom, and why
Follow their guidance on next steps
gather: A short written summary of the situation
The specific question or decision needed
escalation.document: Log the escalation, who you contacted, and the outcome in Contractors Cloud.
escalation.ifFails: If your lead isn't available, use the Internal Escalation template and note it needs a response — don't let the claim sit idle.
